work: The Bartered Bride (Prodaná nevěsta), Overture
premiere_or_publication: Opera premiered 30 May 1866, Provisional Theatre, Prague; final version 1870

work: Hungarian Dance No. 5 in G minor, WoO 1
premiere_or_publication: Published for piano four hands in 1869 (the first two books of the Hungarian Dances); orchestrated later
dating_note: Brahms met the violinist Reményi in 1850, which introduced him to csárdás music, and the first sets of Hungarian Dances were published in 1869; when he arranged No. 5 is not documented, so the range runs from 1850. The tune is Béla Kéler's.

recording.why: Orchestral version is common; piano four-hands original is also fine.

trivia: Brahms mistakenly thought the tune was a folk song, but it comes from the csárdás 'Bártfai emlék' by Béla Kéler. It is the best known of his twenty-one Hungarian Dances.

work: Romeo and Juliet, Fantasy-Overture (final 1880 version)
premiere_or_publication: First version premiered March 1870 in Moscow; final version completed by 10 September 1880, premiered 1886 in Tbilisi
dating_note: Written in three versions (1869, 1870, 1880). The 1880 version, with a new ending, is the one usually played, so it is carded as 1880 with the range reaching back to 1869.

trivia: The subject was suggested by Mily Balakirev, who criticised the first draft and prompted Tchaikovsky to rewrite it twice. The final version, with a revised ending, was not premiered until 1886.
